knowledge.title: Binary
knowledge.explanation: Binary is a number system that uses only two digits: 0 and 1. Computers represent data using binary because electronic circuits can work with two states, commonly described as off and on.
knowledge.example: The binary number 101 represents 5 in denary: 4 + 0 + 1 = 5.

knowledge.title: Bit and byte
knowledge.explanation: A bit is one binary digit: either 0 or 1. A byte is a group of 8 bits. A byte can represent 256 different bit patterns because 2⁸ = 256.
knowledge.example: One byte: 01000001.

knowledge.title: Algorithm
knowledge.explanation: An algorithm is a finite sequence of clear steps used to solve a problem or complete a task. A good algorithm has a defined start and finish and produces the intended result.
knowledge.example: To find the largest of two numbers: input both numbers, compare them, then output the larger number.

knowledge.title: Variable
knowledge.explanation: A variable is a named location used by a program to store a value. The value can change while the program runs.
knowledge.example: score = 10 stores the value 10 in a variable named score.

knowledge.title: Array
knowledge.explanation: An array is a data structure that stores several values under one name. Each value is an element, and its position is identified by an index. In many languages, array indexing begins at 0.
knowledge.example: marks = [72, 81, 65] stores three marks in one array.

knowledge.title: Selection
knowledge.explanation: Selection is a programming construct that chooses which instruction or block of instructions to run based on a condition. Common forms include IF, IF-ELSE and nested IF statements.
knowledge.example: IF temperature > 20 THEN output 'Warm' ELSE output 'Cool'.

knowledge.title: Iteration
knowledge.explanation: Iteration is a programming construct that repeats a set of instructions. A condition-controlled loop repeats while a condition is true; a count-controlled loop repeats a set number of times.
knowledge.example: A loop can add each number in an array to a running total.

knowledge.title: Photosynthesis
knowledge.explanation: Photosynthesis is the process by which green plants use light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water. Chlorophyll in the chloroplasts absorbs the light energy. Oxygen is released.
knowledge.example: Word equation: carbon dioxide + water → glucose + oxygen (using light energy).

knowledge.title: Alkanes
knowledge.explanation: Alkanes are saturated hydrocarbons. They contain only carbon and hydrogen atoms, with single covalent bonds between carbon atoms. The general formula for straight-chain alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.
knowledge.example: Methane is CH₄ and ethane is C₂H₆.

knowledge.title: Alkenes
knowledge.explanation: Alkenes are unsaturated hydrocarbons because they contain at least one carbon–carbon double bond. The general formula for a straight-chain alkene with one double bond is CₙH₂ₙ.
knowledge.example: Ethene is C₂H₄. Alkenes decolourise orange bromine water.

knowledge.title: Intermolecular forces and boiling point
knowledge.explanation: When molecules are larger, the intermolecular attractions between them are generally stronger. More energy is then needed to separate the molecules, so the boiling point generally increases.
knowledge.example: For a homologous series such as alkanes, boiling point generally increases as the carbon chain gets longer.

knowledge.title: The water cycle
knowledge.explanation: The water cycle describes the continuous movement of water. Water evaporates, water vapour cools and condenses into clouds, and water returns to the surface as precipitation. It can then collect in bodies of water or flow over and through the ground.

knowledge.title: Central processing unit (CPU)
knowledge.explanation: The central processing unit (CPU) processes instructions. It uses the fetch–decode–execute cycle: it fetches an instruction from memory, decodes what it means, then executes it. The control unit coordinates activity, while the arithmetic logic unit (ALU) performs calculations and logical operations.
knowledge.example: A CPU can fetch an instruction to add two values, decode the instruction, then use the ALU to carry it out.

knowledge.title: Random access memory (RAM)
knowledge.explanation: RAM is volatile memory that temporarily stores programs and data currently being used by the computer. Its contents are lost when the power is switched off.
knowledge.example: A document being edited may be held in RAM while it is open.

knowledge.title: Read-only memory (ROM)
knowledge.explanation: ROM is non-volatile memory. It stores instructions or firmware that a device needs, such as code used during start-up. Its contents are retained when power is switched off.
knowledge.example: A computer can use firmware stored in ROM during start-up.

knowledge.title: Cache memory
knowledge.explanation: Cache is small, very fast memory close to or inside the CPU. It keeps copies of frequently used data and instructions so the CPU may access them faster than retrieving them from main memory.
knowledge.example: The CPU may find a recently used instruction in cache instead of fetching it from RAM.

knowledge.title: Data validation
knowledge.explanation: Validation checks whether input data follows specified rules. It can check range, length, type, format or presence. Validation does not prove that data is factually correct.
knowledge.example: A mark-entry system may reject a mark outside the permitted range of 0 to 100.

knowledge.title: Data verification
knowledge.explanation: Verification checks that data has been copied or entered accurately by comparing it with the original source. It helps reduce transcription errors but does not prove that the original data is correct.
knowledge.example: With double-entry verification, a user enters the same email address twice and the system compares the entries.

knowledge.title: Software testing
knowledge.explanation: Software testing checks whether a program behaves as expected. Normal test data checks typical valid input, boundary test data checks values at the edges of an allowed range, and erroneous test data checks invalid input.
knowledge.example: For a permitted age range of 1 to 120, boundary tests include 1 and 120; erroneous tests could include 0 and 121.

knowledge.title: Primary key
knowledge.explanation: A primary key is a field, or combination of fields, that uniquely identifies each record in a database table. A primary key value must not be duplicated or left empty.
knowledge.example: A pupil table could use a unique pupil ID as its primary key.

knowledge.title: LAN and WAN
knowledge.explanation: A local area network (LAN) connects devices across a limited area, such as a home, school or office. A wide area network (WAN) connects networks over a much larger geographical area.
knowledge.example: A school computer room may use a LAN; the internet is a large example of a WAN.

knowledge.title: Encryption
knowledge.explanation: Encryption converts readable data (plaintext) into an unreadable form (ciphertext) using an encryption method and key. Decryption converts it back for an authorised recipient with the appropriate key.
knowledge.example: A messaging service can encrypt a message so that someone who intercepts the ciphertext cannot easily read the original message.

knowledge.title: HTML and CSS
knowledge.explanation: HTML describes the structure and content of a web page, such as headings, paragraphs, links and images. CSS controls how that content is presented, including colours, spacing and layout.
knowledge.example: An HTML h1 element creates a main heading; a CSS rule can change that heading's colour.

knowledge.title: Atomic structure
knowledge.explanation: An atom has a tiny central nucleus containing protons and usually neutrons. Electrons occupy regions around the nucleus. Protons have a positive charge, electrons have a negative charge and neutrons have no charge.
knowledge.example: A neutral atom has the same number of protons and electrons.

knowledge.title: Atomic number
knowledge.explanation: The atomic number of an element is the number of protons in the nucleus of each of its atoms. The proton number identifies the element.
knowledge.example: Every carbon atom has 6 protons, so carbon has atomic number 6.

knowledge.title: Isotopes
knowledge.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons. They have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
knowledge.example: Carbon-12 and carbon-14 both have 6 protons, but they have different numbers of neutrons.

knowledge.title: Covalent bonding
knowledge.explanation: A covalent bond forms when atoms share one or more pairs of electrons. This commonly occurs between non-metal atoms.
knowledge.example: In a hydrogen molecule, two hydrogen atoms share a pair of electrons.

knowledge.title: Ionic bonding
knowledge.explanation: Ionic bonding involves the transfer of electrons from one atom to another, producing positive and negative ions. The ions are held together by electrostatic attraction between opposite charges.
knowledge.example: In sodium chloride, sodium forms a positive ion and chlorine forms a negative ion.

knowledge.title: Neutralisation
knowledge.explanation: Neutralisation happens when an acid reacts with a base or alkali. An acid reacting with an alkali produces a salt and water.
knowledge.example: Hydrochloric acid + sodium hydroxide → sodium chloride + water.

knowledge.title: Exothermic and endothermic reactions
knowledge.explanation: An exothermic reaction transfers energy to the surroundings, so the surroundings usually become warmer. An endothermic reaction takes in energy from the surroundings, so the surroundings usually become cooler.
knowledge.example: Combustion is exothermic; some thermal decomposition reactions are endothermic.

knowledge.title: Homologous series
knowledge.explanation: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula. Members have similar chemical properties, and successive members differ by CH₂.
knowledge.example: Alkanes form a homologous series with the general formula CₙH₂ₙ₊₂.

knowledge.title: Diffusion
knowledge.explanation: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration, down a concentration gradient.
knowledge.example: Oxygen can diffuse from the air sacs in the lungs into the blood.

knowledge.title: Osmosis
knowledge.explanation: Osmosis is the net movement of water molecules through a selectively permeable membrane from a region of higher water concentration to a region of lower water concentration.
knowledge.example: Water can move into a plant cell by osmosis when the surrounding solution is more dilute.

knowledge.title: Enzymes
knowledge.explanation: Enzymes are biological catalysts that speed up reactions without being used up. A substrate binds to an enzyme's active site. High temperatures or unsuitable pH can change the active site's shape and reduce enzyme activity.
knowledge.example: Amylase is an enzyme that breaks down starch.

knowledge.title: Aerobic respiration
knowledge.explanation: Aerobic respiration releases energy from glucose using oxygen. In words: glucose + oxygen → carbon dioxide + water. The released energy is used for cell activities.
knowledge.example: Muscle cells use energy released by aerobic respiration during activity.

knowledge.title: Cell membrane
knowledge.explanation: The cell membrane forms the boundary of a cell and controls the movement of substances into and out of the cell. It is selectively permeable.
knowledge.example: Oxygen and other small substances can move across the cell membrane.

knowledge.title: Percentage
knowledge.explanation: A percentage is a way of expressing a number as a fraction of 100. The symbol % means 'per hundred'.
knowledge.example: 25% means 25 out of 100, which is equal to one quarter.

knowledge.title: Fractions
knowledge.explanation: A fraction represents part of a whole or a ratio of quantities. The numerator is the top number and the denominator is the bottom number; the denominator cannot be zero.
knowledge.example: In 3/4, 3 is the numerator and 4 is the denominator.
